stories.title: New Vaccine Shows Early Signs Of Stopping Cancer Spread
stories.summary:
Moderna and Merck reported that their experimental personalized mRNA vaccine, Intismeran, met its primary and secondary goals in a late-stage trial for high-risk melanoma. The treatment was administered alongside Merck’s Keytruda.

The companies said the combination therapy kept the cancer from returning for longer periods and reduced the risk of it spreading to other parts of the body. These results indicate early signs that the vaccine can help stop the progression of the disease in late-stage patients.

stories.title: Telemundo executive among five Americans killed in Kenya helicopter crash
stories.summary:
A sightseeing helicopter crashed in Kenya on Wednesday, killing seven people. The victims included five American citizens and two others.

The U.S. State Department confirmed the deaths of the Americans. Among them was Jose Alberto Suarez, a Telemundo executive who served as president and general manager.

BBC reporting identified additional victims, including Michele Sensi-Contugi and his wife Stephany Hollihan. The pilot and another passenger were also killed in the crash.

stories.title: Trump says Iran talks could resume ‘at some point,’ threatens ‘draconian’ sanctions
stories.summary:
President Donald Trump said on Wednesday that the United States could resume peace talks with Iran “at some point,” while warning of “draconian” sanctions if Tehran does not change its behavior. The remarks came after he initially stated Tuesday that U.S. negotiators were not in contact with their Iranian counterparts.

Trump described the current status quo in the conflict as “very good” and expressed confidence that concerns over the Strait of Hormuz are being addressed. Al Jazeera reported that Trump announced what it called the “most crushing” Iran sanctions, underscoring a dual-track approach combining diplomatic openness with economic pressure.

stories.title: Longtime publisher of Stars and Stripes to retire, citing differences with Pentagon leadership
stories.summary:
The longtime publisher of Stars and Stripes has announced his retirement, ending a decades-long career with the military newspaper. The departure comes amid growing tensions between the publication's leadership and the Pentagon.

Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth's administration has moved to exert editorial control over the paper, citing efforts to eliminate what it describes as "woke distractions." The publisher cited differences with Pentagon leadership as the reason for his exit.

The resignation highlights a broader push by the Trump administration to influence military media. It marks a significant shift in the relationship between the armed forces and their official newspaper.

stories.title: Miranda Devine: Jon Ossoff’s disgustingly sly and sexist attack on Trump aide Natalie Harp backfires big time
stories.summary:
Democratic Senator Jon Ossoff’s criticism of Trump aide Natalie Harp has drawn sharp pushback, with columnist Miranda Devine describing the attack as “disgustingly sly and sexist.”

Devine questioned whether Ossoff implied that a hard-working single professional woman could not succeed without sleeping with her boss.

Harp, one of Trump’s longest-serving and most loyal aides, was thrust back into the spotlight after Ossoff noted her closeness to the president. BBC coverage identified Harp as a key figure in the administration, while New York Post commentary framed the controversy around gendered assumptions about professional success.

stories.title: Why is ‘mushroom killer’ Erin Patterson back in court? – video
stories.summary:
Erin Patterson, known as the “mushroom killer,” is back in court this week as three Victorian judges hear her appeal against a triple murder conviction. The case involves the deaths of three relatives who ate beef wellington laced with death cap mushrooms.

The Court of Appeal will also consider a separate challenge from Victoria’s director of public prosecutions, who is seeking to remove any chance of parole for Patterson. Prosecutors are asking that she be sentenced to life in prison without the possibility of release.

Patterson argues her mushroom murder convictions should be quashed due to what she describes as a “catastrophic” failure of justice. Meanwhile, prosecutors have stated there is no indication Patterson had an “innocent interest” in mushrooms, according to ABC News.

stories.title: Australia politics live: Israel ambassador says to ‘respect the process’ after IDF rules out criminal investigation of Zomi Frankcom killing
stories.summary:
Israel’s ambassador to Australia has urged the public to “respect the process” after the Israeli Defense Forces ruled out a criminal investigation into the killing of Australian aid worker Zomi Frankcom.

Ambassador Hillel Newman defended the IDF’s findings, which cleared its soldiers of criminal wrongdoing. He stated that the report should not be subjected to “political attacks” if it does not align with someone’s political agenda.

The comments come amid growing domestic controversy over the incident. Greens leader Larissa Waters described the situation as outrageous and suggested that sending the Israeli ambassador home should be considered.

stories.summary:
House House, the Melbourne studio behind Untitled Goose Game, has released Big Walk, a new title centered on exploration and conversation rather than traditional objectives. The game encourages players to walk together with friends, using movement as a framework for social interaction.

The Guardian’s review highlights the developers’ emphasis on finding joy in simple shared experiences. During an interview session at the studio, the team took reporters on a hike through local scrubland to demonstrate the game's core philosophy of unhurried exploration.

According to the article, the experience often leads to unexpected emotional moments. The developers describe some player stories as “punch-in-the-gut beautiful,” suggesting that the lack of rigid goals allows for more organic and meaningful connections between participants.

stories.title: The Blood of Dawnwalker – save your family while becoming what you hate
stories.summary:
The Blood of Dawnwalker is a dark fantasy role-playing game developed by some of the talent behind The Witcher 3. It follows Coen, who is human by day and vampire by night, as he navigates difficult choices to save his family.

Set in the 14th century in the fictional land of Vale Sangora, the game takes place in a Carpathian valley of wetlands, mountains, and forests that is cut off from the rest of the world. The region is under the rule of a vicio, creating an isolated and oppressive environment for the protagonist.

The story begins in the 1300s but could span centuries through upcoming sequels, suggesting the start of an epic saga. Players will experience Coen's transformation into what he hates while attempting to protect his loved ones.

The device is positioned as an entirely new variant within Samsung's foldable lineup, offering substantial processing power and battery life alongside its distinctive physical design.

stories.title: DOST, Bukidnon push P10-M ‘smart’ farming initiative
stories.summary:
The provincial government of Bukidnon and the Department of Science and Technology (DOST) have launched a nearly P10-million “smart” agricultural monitoring initiative. The project aims to equip local farmers and officials with timely data to better manage climate-related risks.

stories.summary:
Rwanda-backed rebels have entered Goma, a city in the Democratic Republic of Congo that had served as a safe haven for displaced residents. The advance followed reports of gunfire and shelling after rebel forces overran Congolese troops.
